messages:
marie: FYI deploybot paused rc-20/1.28.0 canary — vuln scan found a high severity issue in a transitive build dependency (details below). recommending quick decision on regional carve-out or full rollback.

deploy-bot: [automated] Pipeline ACTION: vuln-scan FAILED. Artifact: docs-renderer-1.2.3.tar.gz. Issue: CVE-2026-0457 (high) in prism-highlight (transitive via doc-builder). Affected stages: canary -> global rollout. Blocking global promotion.

ashok: Did the scanner confirm this is present in runtime code, or only in build-time tooling that leaked into the package?

elaine: It's showing up in the bundled pre-rendered HTML assets — the vuln originates in the syntax highlight lib used by the doc generator, but the compiled JS ships in the artifact. So technically in artifact delivered to customers.

devsec: Need repro that the shipped JS is exploitable in customer context. If it's only used for static rendering without eval, risk might be lower. But legal/reg compliance in EU flagged license mismatch too. We need mitigation commitments before any carve-out.

legal: If EU regulators consider this an export/compliance issue we cannot ship there without review. We need scope of exposure and timeline for remediation.

marie: Option A: full rollback until we rebuild without doc-builder (ETA ~2h). Option B: carve-out — limit rollout to non-EU regions (us-west, us-east, ap-south) with a hard stop for enterprise accounts and EU customers, push hotfix within 24h, and notify stakeholders. Which path?

ashok: My preference is Option B if devsec + legal sign off on compensating controls. We need a precise checklist to allow regional carve-out.

devsec: Compensating controls we require: 1) exclude eu-* regions from this canary 2) disable any customer-supplied content rendering that could trigger the vuln 3) schedule hotfix/rebuild within 24h and run regression evals 4) obtain written ack from Legal for EU exclusion. If those are met, we can approve a regional rollout for non-EU.

elaine: I can run a rebuild job that drops the doc-builder step and re-generates the static assets without the vulnerable library. Rebuild + test pipeline ~2h. I can also trigger a scoped rollout in deploybot.

release-ci: Suggested command to set scope:```/deploybot promote canary --artifact docs-renderer-1.2.3.tar.gz --scope us-west,us-east,ap-south --exclude eu-* --hold-accounts enterprise --requires-approvals devsec,legal```deploybot will enforce gating and require approvals before expanding.

deploy-bot: To confirm: promotion blocked until explicit approvals provided. Use `/deploybot approve <thread_ts> <approver>` once controls are in place. Audit log will capture scope and approvers.

legal: I'll review the exclusion language and send a short exception approval if we can guarantee no EU delivery and we get a hotfix within 24 hours.

ashok: OK — plan: Elaine triggers rebuild now, I will request devsec + legal approval in this thread once rebuild artifacts are validated. Marie will draft customer-facing note for enterprise/EU hold. If approvals land, proceed with scoped canary to us-west/us-east.

marie: :eyes: drafting release note now and pinging accounts team to delay EU customer notifications until patch is ready.

devsec: I'll run an exploit check on the rebuilt artifact and post results here. If green, I will +1 for scoped rollout.

ashok: thanks — holding global rollout. tagging incident page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RELEASE-3124 and will update timeline in 30m.

release-ci: Noted. I'll watch for approvals and will not expand rollout without explicit /deploybot approve entries. :thumbsup:
